method: Differential whole-source review against reviewed Windows GNU SSE4.1: normalized all2006 instructions and resolved GNU numeric/MASM anonymous or named labels to instruction-index branch targets. Inspected all four residual instruction differences and full MASM directive/data inventory. Equivalent instructions not independently serial-reread.

equivalence_accounting.normalization: Hex numbers converted to integer; whitespace collapsed; explicit +rip removed for text comparison only; prefetch byte ptr spelling normalized. Directives/data excluded and separately inspected.

findings: Both scalar compression functions spell movd xmm3,r9 and movd xmm4,r8 where GNU uses movq. These four r64 operand forms are preserved as actual source differences; MASM acceptance and64-bit transfer encoding require object/build verification. No counter truncation or build failure claimed from spelling alone.

All other2002 normalized instructions including stack argument offsets, register preservation and restores match Windows GNU. All conditional/unconditional branch destinations match after resolving anonymous @F/@B labels and named labels to instruction positions.

PUBLIC plus paired PROC/ENDP expose both symbol spellings for all three entry points. CODE segment/loop alignment16 and READONLY .rdata segment with ALIGN64 replace GNU directives. No FRAME/unwind annotations observed.

DUP declarations expand repeated IV/block-length/counter-step words. CMP_MSB_MASK allocates eight32-bit masks whereas GNU has four: inspected SSE loads consume16 bytes, so extra constant storage alone does not establish semantic error. Rotate byte masks and IV values match on source inspection.

Stack64 alignment for hash-many,528-byte reservation and XMM6..15 saves remain as GNU; scalar functions preserve seven actually used nonvolatile XMM registers in120-byte frames. Compile-time and runtime validation remain separate.
limits: No MASM build, object disassembly, Windows execution, throughput or sanitizer proof. Upstream source not imported; pHash/ASAN deferred.
